what_this_is: Rows where one certification ASSERTS a requirement another DENIES. The only defect class in the corpus no other instrument covers: every gate here checks a row against a STANDARD, nothing checked a row against another ROW.
headline: ONE candidate, and it is NOT a contradiction. Zero real contradictions remain.
why_it_is_not_three: The sweep found three before batch A. Batch A rewrote aia-independence-wherever-practicable and ia-internal-auditor-limited-independence-remedy, and the ISMS-F fix replaced auditor-objectivity, which resolved two of the three. The survivor is the one below.

denial.says: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2 a) requires the organization to define the audit criteria and scope for each audit. It does not require audit objectives.

assertion.says: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 9.2.2 ... the organization shall define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit

candidates.verdict: NOT A CONTRADICTION. Both rows are correct and the STANDARDS differ.

verification.self_test: 27001:2022 contains 'internal audit' -- the search was working before any absence was reported.
verification.27001:2022: PRESENT: 'define the audit criteria and scope for each audit'. ABSENT from the whole standard: 'audit objectives'. Only one line in 27001 mentions 'for each audit' and it is clause 9.2.2 a), without objectives.
verification.42001:2023: clause 9.2.2 a) read off the PDF: 'define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit'. Objectives present.
verification.note_on_method: A clause-address extraction of 27001 cl.9.2.2 returned ZERO characters -- the licence-watermark column defeats a heading match on that document. An empty extraction is a FAILURE and not an answer, so nothing was concluded from it and the question was settled by phrase search with a self-test instead.

candidates.action: NONE. This is a real divergence between two harmonised siblings, at exactly the kind of point an auditor finds examinable: 42001 adds audit objectives where 27001 does not. Both certifications report their own standard accurately.
candidates.worth_noting: This is the valuable kind of false positive. It fires because the vocabulary genuinely overlaps and the claims genuinely differ, and reading it confirms both the instrument and the content. A sweep that never surfaced anything like this would be one nobody could trust.

instrument_notes.regression_control_moved_to_a_fixture: Its first version asserted that auditor-objectivity was surfaced from the LIVE corpus. That worked once and failed on the next run -- because the row had been FIXED, so the contradiction no longer existed. A control that depends on a defect remaining in production forbids repairing it, which is the shape of the `migration tip vs disk` invariant. The control now runs the matcher against a fixture holding the original text of both rows, and reports the live status separately.
instrument_notes.length_bias: The first threshold required four shared distinctive terms and returned 50 candidates, none of them the founding case. auditor-objectivity is seven words; once auditor, audit and requirement are stopworded as corpus-frequent, two distinctive terms remain. The threshold is now relative to the shorter row, floor two.
instrument_notes.what_it_cannot_do: It matches vocabulary. Two rows can share vocabulary and not contradict -- this candidate is exactly that -- and two rows can contradict sharing none. It generates candidates and decides nothing.
